mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the real discount rate, thereby increasing the present value of expected corporate earnings and pushing the S&P 500 20-day forward return to the negative.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of FEDFUNDS > 4.0 regimes, or FEDFUNDS decline occurs but has no statistically significant effect on SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +0.5% in a month following a rate hike, the market anticipates continued inflation, causing the S&P 500 to decline over the next 60 trading days as investors demand higher yields.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > +0.5% and previous FEDFUNDS > 5.0%
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not statistically different from the mean of the prior 12 months (p > 0.05) when trigger is met, or the CPIAUCSL change is not followed by a 60-day SPX decline in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in PAYEMS (labor market additions) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (unemployment) indicates a tight labor market, which typically precedes equity market overvaluation and drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > +10% and UNRATE monthly change < -0.5%
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when trigger is met in >50% of observations, or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in GDPC1 (goods orders) of at least 5% for three consecutive months is interpreted as weakening demand, which reduces growth expectations and produces a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as the market anticipates a near-term correction.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not statistically different from zero when the trigger is met (p > 0.05), or the effect persists for less than 2 months on average.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls by more than 8% in a month, it signals supply-side weakness that, if persistent, elevates risk premia and drives a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return, especially in a regime of low inflation.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negatively correlated with INDPRO changes in the trigger regime (Spearman's rho < -0.2).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both HOUST (housing starts) and RSAFS (retail sales) above 5% and 3% monthly increases, respectively, for two months, creates an overbuilding and overstocking cycle that the market interprets as a near-term recession, producing a positive 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > +5% and RSAFS monthly change > +3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly different from the mean of the prior 12 months when trigger is met (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a declining UNRATE below 4% coupled with a sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS of at least 8% suggests a tight labor market that amplifies wage growth expectations and drives a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS monthly change > +8% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative when the trigger is met in the post-softening regime (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A long-term upward trend in the 12-month moving average of FEDFUNDS is associated with higher long-term discount rates and lower equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns even in the absence of short-term shocks.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not consistently positive when FEDFUNDS MA12 is rising (Wilcoxon signed-rank test p < 0.05).
